bullets: Un sistema rápido cruza el lunes con humedad y dinámica limitadas: solo chubascos ligeros y acumulaciones mínimas en terreno alto.
Una cresta de alta presión trae tiempo seco desde el martes hasta al menos media semana.
Para Thanksgiving y el fin de semana sigue posible un patrón más activo, pero los ensambles no coinciden (confianza baja).

sections.Key Messages:
- Snow will begin along the northern Divide this evening,
  lingering through Sunday morning. Snow totals of 10-15 inches
  are expected for the Park and Elkhead mountains, with 4-8
  inches across the Flat Tops and Central Divide Mountains.
- Winds gusting 40 to 50 mph are expected with this system this
  evening through Saturday night, leading to blowing and
  drifting snow and difficult driving conditions over the
  mountain passes.
- An unsettled pattern looks to continue into next week with
  potential for more mountain snow by mid week, but details
  remain uncertain.
sections.Discussion:
Issued at 1104 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026
DRY AND MILD THIS AFTERNOON:
Mid and high clouds continue to spill in from the northwest as
a strong atmospheric river carried by a low pressure trough
pushes into the Pacific Northwest as seen on satellite imagery.
This moisture is being carried up and over a high pressure ridge
sitting over the Desert Southwest but is showing signs of
breaking down. Conditions this afternoon will remain dry with
showers increasing this evening over the northern mountains as
this moisture moves into the northern portion of our CWA.
Anticipate mild temperatures about 5 degrees above normal this
afternoon.
MOUNTAIN SNOWFALL TONIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY NIGHT:
A strong 140 kt jet will accompany this rather robust shortwave
as it tracks through the Intermountain West and Northern
Rockies with the jet setting up tonight over northern Utah into
southwest Colorado, with the northern and central Colorado
mountains in the more favored area for strong lift. Specific
humidity climbs above 4 g/kg with PWAT anomalies above 200
percent of normal across the north so even though we are on the
tail end of this AR moisture as it moves further inland, we will
have plenty to work with. The strongest period of forcing looks
to occur Saturday morning into the early afternoon, with the
highest snowfall rates expected between 5 am and 5 pm Saturday.
This is a favorable setup for strong northwest orographics in
addition to the dynamics and QG forcing during this time. Post-
Thanksgiving travel will be impacted during the morning and
evening commutes on Saturday so be prepared for difficult winter
driving conditions with blowing snow also contributing to
reduced visibilities as winds are expected to gust 40 to 50 mph
over the higher terrain and passes. The lower elevations could
see winds gusting 30 to 40 mph as well at times but look to
remain rain if anything. The impacts will be in the northern and
central mountains with the Park Range on track to receive 10 to
15 inches. Probabilities of over a foot of snow is highest in
the Park Range with chances 70 to 80 percent, so the Winter
Storm Warning remains on track with Winter Weather Advisories
for the Flattops and Gore and Elk Mountains including the I-70
mountain corridor through Vail and Vail Pass where 4 to 8 inches
of snow is expected. Timing of these winter highlights is 5 pm
today through 5 am Sunday as snow looks to continue through
early Sunday morning.
SUNDAY AND BEYOND:
A transitory ridge will slide in for Sunday and Monday with
drier conditions expected. Some high clouds will continue to
pass overhead due to another system moving into the Pacific
Northwest but this one doesn't appear to impact us much as it
tracks to our northwest as it moves inland and weakens. The next
potential weather maker to watch for is another AR and low
pressure trough that moves onto the west coast Tuesday and
potentially brings more mountain snowfall to our region during
the mid week timeframe. There is still quite a bit of model
uncertainty with this system with differences in timing and
storm track. The GFS takes a more southerly track with this low
becoming closed off and splitting as it tracks south of the Four
Corners through Arizona and New Mexico Wednesday evening
through Thursday. The ECMWF track is a bit further north coming
in as an open wave trough but still favoring the southern
mountains. Model guidance remains in relatively poor agreement,
with significant spread. The southerly track does increase
potential for atmospheric river moisture to accompany this
system. However, the exact track of this system can make the
difference between a solid mountain snowfall and seeing little
to no snow at all. We shall have to wait and see how the
forecast for this system develops over the coming days.
sections.Aviation:
Issued at 1019 AM MST Fri Nov 27 2026
SCT to BKN cloud cover will continue to propagate through the
area today. Clouds will begin to lower and thicken into the
afternoon and evening hours. Moisture enters the region tonight,
with precipitation chances hitting KHDN first (~01Z), then
spreading southward by ~06-08Z. These precipitation chances will
mainly be confined to KHDN, KEGE, KRIL, KASE, KGUC, and KTEX. At
the above mentioned terminals, it is possible that cigs fall
below ILS breakpoints and flight categories will be less than
VFR at times. At terminals where precipitation is not observed,
VFR conditions are likely to prevail. Additionally, higher
sustained wind speeds and periodic gustiness should not be ruled
out as this system traverses the area.
